name: schedule-risk
title: Schedule risk (Monte Carlo)
description: Monte Carlo schedule risk of a P6 project on this server's CPM engine: finish dates at p10, p50, p80 and p90, the chance to finish on time, the p80 buffer, milestones, the activities that drive the finish most often and the assumptions (read only). Use when the user asks how likely the finish date is, for a risk analysis, a confidence level or a schedule contingency.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: seed
args.description: Random seed: the same seed gives the same result

template:
Schedule risk of project {project}: a Monte Carlo simulation of {iterations} iterations (seed {seed}) on this server's CPM engine gives the finish dates at p10, p50, p80 and p90, the chance to finish on time, the p80 buffer, the milestones and the activities most often on the critical path. Read only: nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. cv = p6_cpm_validate(project="{project}", limit=5): the engine against the last F9: the simulation runs on it.
2. rk = p6_schedule_risk(project="{project}", iterations={iterations}, seed={seed}, limit=15): Monte Carlo: finish percentiles, chances, milestones, drivers, weeks.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The caveat of the result is copied as it is, in the user's language: never present the percentiles as a
  forecast without it.
- The same project, iterations and seed give the same figures: say which seed was used, and run again with
  another seed only when the user asks.
- Other ranges (by Activity ID, WBS or activity code, or three-point estimates in UDFs) are arguments of
  p6_schedule_risk: use them only when the user gives the ranges, and say which were used.

# Schedule risk of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Read only: nothing was written to the database.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. The simulation starts from out of date dates until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: trusted]
Warning: this server's CPM engine does not reproduce the last F9 of this project (match rate {match_rate}), so the simulated dates may not follow P6's. Run the logic-date-integrity skill to see the differences before using these figures.
[end if]

## Finish

- Deterministic finish (the engine, durations unchanged): {det_finish}, {det_activity}; last F9: {stored_finish}.
- P10 {p10}; P50 {p50}; P80 {p80}; P90 {p90}.
- Chance to finish by the deterministic finish: {on_time_det}. Must finish by {must_finish}: chance {on_time_must}.
- P80 buffer: {p80_buffer} working days of the project calendar after the deterministic finish.

## Milestones

[table: milestones]

## Drivers

Share of the iterations in which each open activity sat on the critical path (the chain of links that set each start, back from the project finish); On today's path = on the critical path of the deterministic run. Min and Max are the remaining durations drawn from.

[table: drivers]

## Finish dates per week

[table: weeks]

## Assumptions

- {iterations_run} iterations, seed {seed_used}, engine version {engine_version}. Engine match rate with the last F9: {match_rate}.
- Remaining duration of {n_drawn} open activities drawn from a triangular range of {d_min} % (minimum), {d_mode} % (most likely) and {d_max} % (maximum) of the remaining duration.
[if: iterations_note]
- Iterations: {iterations_note}.
[end if]
- {caveat}

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_schedule_risk says the project has no data date or that the network has a loop: repeat its message and
  stop (P6 cannot schedule a loop either).

## Warnings (fixed wording in report.md)

- schedule_state.stale is true: keep the warning.
- cv.trusted is false: keep the warning that the engine does not reproduce the last F9, and point to the
  logic-date-integrity skill.
- iterations_note is not null: keep its line (fewer iterations ran on a large network, or the number asked was
  outside 100 to 5000).

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. cv.schedule_state.data_date = rk.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. cv.match_rate = rk.engine.match_rate (same engine).

If a group differs, the database changed between the calls: run the two calls again once. If it still
differs, say which group differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you: no
  percentile, chance or buffer is worked out from the weeks or from two dates.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (milestones 10, drivers 15, weeks
  20). When rk has more pages of drivers (next_offset not null) the drivers table ends with "Showing the
  first <returned> of <total> activities.", both numbers copied from rk.
- Activities are written "Activity ID - name".
- The caveat is copied as it is (translated with the report), never left out.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Schedule risk (Monte Carlo)

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. cv = p6_cpm_validate(project="{project}", limit=5): the engine against the last F9: the simulation runs on it.
2. rk = p6_schedule_risk(project="{project}", iterations={iterations}, seed={seed}, limit=15): Monte Carlo: finish percentiles, chances, milestones, drivers, weeks.

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {iterations}: Monte Carlo iterations (100 to 5000), as given
- {seed}: Random seed: the same seed gives the same result, as given

## Units

- wd: working days of each activity's calendar
- wd proj: working days of the project calendar
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- %: percent
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | rk.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date |
| last_f9 | rk.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last schedule run (F9) in P6 |
| stale | rk.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | changed by this server after the last F9 |
| match_rate | cv.match_rate |  | n2 | n/a | share of open activities the engine reproduces (1.00 = all) |
| trusted | cv.trusted |  | flag | n/a | match rate at least 0.99 |
| det_finish | rk.deterministic.finish |  | datetime | n/a | finish of the engine with unchanged durations |
| det_activity | rk.['deterministic.finish_activity', 'deterministic.finish_activity_name'] |  | id_name | n/a | finish activity |
| stored_finish | rk.deterministic.stored_finish |  | datetime | n/a | finish of the last F9 |
| p10 | rk.finish.p10 |  | datetime | n/a | finish reached in 10 % of the iterations |
| p50 | rk.finish.p50 |  | datetime | n/a | finish reached in 50 % |
| p80 | rk.finish.p80 |  | datetime | n/a | finish reached in 80 % |
| p90 | rk.finish.p90 |  | datetime | n/a | finish reached in 90 % |
| must_finish | rk.must_finish |  | datetime | none | must finish by date |
| on_time_det | rk.on_time_probability.deterministic_pct | % | pct1 | n/a | iterations finishing by the deterministic finish |
| on_time_must | rk.on_time_probability.must_finish_pct | % | pct1 | n/a | iterations finishing by the must finish date |
| p80_buffer | rk.p80_buffer_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a | deterministic finish to p80 |
| iterations_run | rk.iterations | count | int | n/a | iterations run |
| iterations_note | rk.iterations_note |  | text | n/a | why fewer or other iterations ran (null: as asked) |
| seed_used | rk.seed |  | int | n/a | random seed |
| engine_version | rk.engine_version |  | int | n/a | version of the engine's rules |
| d_min | rk.distribution.default.min_pct | % | n0 | n/a | default range: minimum, % of the remaining duration |
| d_mode | rk.distribution.default.mode_pct | % | n0 | n/a | most likely |
| d_max | rk.distribution.default.max_pct | % | n0 | n/a | maximum |
| n_drawn | rk.distribution.counts.drawn | count | int | n/a | activities whose remaining duration is drawn |
| caveat | rk.caveat |  | text | n/a | what the estimate leaves out |

## Table milestones

The finish activity, then the open constrained activities.

Rows: rk.milestones, in the order returned, at most 10 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 10 items, add the line: Only the first 10 milestones are shown.
No rows: write 'No milestone.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Deterministic | deterministic |  | datetime | n/a |  |
| P50 | p50 |  | datetime | n/a |  |
| P80 | p80 |  | datetime | n/a |  |
| P90 | p90 |  | datetime | n/a |  |
| On time % | on_time_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| Constraint date | constraint_date |  | datetime | none |  |
| By constraint % | by_constraint_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| P80 buffer (wd) | p80_buffer_wd | wd | n1 | n/a |  |

## Table drivers

Open activities by share of iterations on the critical path.

Rows: rk.rows, in the order returned, at most 15.
When rk.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> activities. (returned and total of rk).
No rows: write 'No activity was critical.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Critical % | criticality_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| On today's path | on_deterministic_path |  | flag | n/a |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Remaining (d) | rem_dur_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Min (d) | min_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Max (d) | max_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |

## Table weeks

Project finish dates per week.

Rows: rk.histogram, in the order returned, at most 20 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 20 items, add the line: Only the first 20 weeks are shown.
No rows: write 'No week.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Week from | week_start |  | date | n/a |  |
| To | week_end |  | date | n/a |  |
| Iterations | count | count | int | n/a |  |
| % | pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| Cumulative % | cum_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- same data date: cv.schedule_state.data_date = rk.schedule_state.data_date
- same engine match rate: cv.match_rate = rk.engine.match_rate
